core_obligations: Set up the contradiction: from an assumed definable equivalence obtain a tree order prec on U_{T_1} with finite support A, chosen to be a subtree, and record that any automorphism fixing A pointwise also fixes prec (proof lines 384-388).

Describe the action: introduce the pieces U_a, L_ab, C_x and show that the stabiliser of A acts transitively on each of them and even with support inside them, using density and weak 2-transitivity (proof lines 390-410).

Determine prec on each piece: on U_a, incomparable points stay incomparable, the case b < c with c prec b is excluded, and otherwise prec agrees with the tree order; on S_ab comparabilities only occur inside a single C_c, and there prec agrees with the tree order (proof lines 416-446).

Exclude the degenerate case: if prec were empty on every U_a and C_c, the union of the pieces would be an antichain satisfying the same first order sentences as the original tree, impossible because its chains are infinite (proof lines 448-455).

Recover the codes: from a piece where the two orders agree, extend the agreement upward, then read off the ramification orders above a point, which are given by first order formulae, so that the two codes coincide after all - contradicting their being distinct (proof lines 457-466).
proof_roadmap: Turn a definable equivalence into a finitely supported tree order on the first tree and analyse it piecewise using the transitive action of the stabiliser (proof lines 384-446).
Rule out the degenerate case, propagate agreement between the orders, and extract the equality of codes from first order definable ramification orders (proof lines 448-466).
difficulty_reason: The theorem compares two countable weakly 2-transitive trees whose maximal chains in the one-point extensions are dense, and asserts that distinct infinite codes force the definable cardinalities of their node sets to be inequivalent, both lying in Delta_5 but not in Delta_4 (statement lines 377-379). The proof assumes an equivalence, which by the theory of definable cardinality gives a tree order on the first node set with a finite support and hence invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of that support, and then analyses that order on the pieces cut out by the support: it shows that on each piece the new order either agrees with the tree order or collapses to an antichain, using automorphisms that swap incomparable points inside the piece (proof lines 384-446). The decisive steps are the exclusion of the all-antichain case, which uses that the assumed order satisfies the same first order sentences and hence has only infinite chains, and the final recovery of the ramification orders above a point, which are first order definable and therefore equal to the codes (proof lines 448-466). H2.

compared: STK-logic-dedekind-delta5 (label 3.1) places the node set of one such tree into Delta_5 and shows it is outside Delta_4 when the tree has infinitely many ramification orders; this theorem compares two trees and separates them by their codes, so it is a different statement that does not duplicate the earlier one.
The cards on 4.1, 4.3 and 4.4 are results about subtrees, templates and local isomorphism of trees and do not assert anything about definable cardinality.
